content_units: You have a credible transition story:   water infrastructure + project coordination + Python   maps well into climate adaptation, flood/stormwater risk, resilience planning, and infrastructure risk analytics. In Melbourne, the strongest fit is likely   climate risk roles tied to infrastructure, water, utilities, consulting, and government  , rather than pure carbon accounting or advanced quant-research roles.

Target salary of   AUD 110k–135k   is realistic within 12 months if you position yourself for   consultant / analyst / advisor / engineer   roles that value domain experience, not just data science depth.
Role   Fit for your background   Likely gap   Salary fit
Climate Risk Analyst   Strong if focused on physical risk, assets, flood, resilience   Climate scenario frameworks; risk reporting   Good
Resilience / Climate Adaptation Consultant   Very strong for water + infrastructure background   Adaptation planning methods; policy literacy   Good
Flood Risk / Catchment Risk Analyst   Excellent direct fit   GIS depth; hazard/risk modelling workflows   Very strong
Infrastructure Risk Engineer   Excellent fit   Enterprise risk frameworks; climate disclosure language   Very strong
Water Resources / Stormwater Analyst with climate focus   Excellent fit   Scenario analysis; analytics storytelling   Very strong
ESG / Physical Climate Risk Consultant   Moderate fit   TCFD/ISSB, financial-materiality language   Good
Natural Hazards / Resilience Advisor   Strong   Emergency/risk governance exposure   Good
Geospatial Climate Data Analyst   Moderate fit if you upskill fast   GIS, remote sensing, stronger Python analytics stack   Possible but more technical
These preserve your sector credibility and make your 6 years count.
These are achievable, but usually need stronger reporting-framework fluency or deeper analytics/GIS capability.
-   Physical climate risk   concepts: hazard, exposure, vulnerability, consequence, risk treatment
-   TCFD   legacy language and current   ISSB/IFRS S2   climate disclosure concepts
- Climate scenario basics:   SSP/RCP  , time horizons, uncertainty, scenario-based planning
- Adaptation and resilience planning for infrastructure assets
This is probably the biggest technical gap for Melbourne roles.
- Spatial joins, buffers, raster vs vector, coordinate systems
- Flood / heat / bushfire / coastal hazard map interpretation
- Basic exposure analysis for infrastructure assets
3) Python for analytics, not software engineering
You likely need “job-ready analyst Python,” not advanced ML.
- Data cleaning and asset-risk scoring workflows
- Reproducible project structure and visual outputs
Hiring managers want people who can translate technical findings into decisions.
- Option appraisal: cost, consequence, adaptation pathway
Months 1-2   Build climate-risk foundation   Learn physical risk concepts; study TCFD/ISSB basics; review Melbourne/Victoria resilience context   1-page transition narrative + glossary notes
Months 3-4   Add GIS capability   Learn QGIS; practice mapping flood/heat exposure; create 2 simple map outputs   Small portfolio project with map visuals
Months 5-6   Upgrade Python for risk workflows   Use pandas/geopandas; build asset exposure analysis; create charts and summary tables   Jupyter case study on infrastructure climate exposure
Months 7-8   Create market-facing portfolio   Build 2-3 projects linked to water/infrastructure; polish LinkedIn and resume   Portfolio PDF / GitHub / slide deck
Months 9-10   Learn advisory/reporting language   Practice risk memos, adaptation options, scenario narratives, disclosure terminology   Sample board-style briefing note
Months 11-12   Interview and apply strategically   Target consulting, water utilities, councils, state agencies; refine STAR stories; apply weekly   20-40 focused applications + interview pack
Portfolio Projects That Will Make You Credible
Option 1:   Flood exposure screening for public assets     Use open flood/hazard layers and sample asset data to rank exposure   Best for direct relevance
Option 2:   Stormwater network climate stress test     Show how rainfall intensity changes may affect drainage/service risk   Strongest bridge from your current background
Option 3:   Heat and critical infrastructure vulnerability map for Melbourne     Combine GIS + climate + prioritisation logic   Good for consulting/government roles
Option 4:   Climate risk register for a water asset portfolio     Translate hazards into likelihood, consequence, controls, and adaptation actions   Best for advisor/consultant roles
How to Position Your Experience on Resume
Use a direct pivot headline, not your old title alone.
Civil Engineer transitioning into Climate Risk Analytics
Water infrastructure professional with 6 years’ experience in asset planning, risk-informed project delivery, stakeholder coordination, and data-supported decision-making.
-   Stakeholder engagement with technical and non-technical teams
- Managed water infrastructure projects from design through delivery
- Led coordination of water infrastructure projects with focus on   asset performance, delivery risk, stakeholder alignment, and resilience considerations  .
- Analysed hydraulic and infrastructure performance data to support   risk identification, service reliability assessment, and evidence-based investment decisions  .
- Worked with multiple stakeholders across projects
- Coordinated engineers, contractors, and client stakeholders to align technical outputs with   risk, compliance, budget, and program objectives  .
- Applied Python for   data cleaning, analysis, and reporting automation  , improving efficiency of engineering assessments and decision support.
Create a dedicated   Climate Risk & Analytics   section:
Resume structure that will work best
Focus your search on employers where your domain background is an advantage:
For Melbourne, your target is most realistic if you land at:
-   Risk / resilience role linked to infrastructure assets
-   AUD 100k–115k   if you enter through a more junior transition role
-   AUD 110k–125k   if you strongly package your water/infrastructure domain expertise
-   AUD 125k–135k   if you secure a role combining technical analysis + project/client coordination
Your project coordination experience is important because it supports movement into   consulting and advisor-level work  , not just analyst-only roles.
- Melbourne focus assumed means roles in   Greater Melbourne / Victoria   rather than remote-only national hiring.
- Salary guidance is based on typical market positioning for infrastructure, consulting, resilience, and analyst/advisor pathways rather than a single employer band.
